text: The model labeled the applicant as low‑risk because three key pieces of information pulled the default probability down. First, the applicant’s revolving‑credit utilization is almost zero (about 0.2 % of the credit limit). Using so little of the available credit signals very responsible borrowing, and this factor alone cut the risk score by a large amount. Second, the applicant is 77 years old. In the data, people at this age tend to have stable financial habits, which further lowered the risk. Finally, a monthly income of $14,500 shows strong earning power, adding another modest reduction. Together, these three inputs pushed the predicted chance of default to just 8.8 %, leading to the “low risk” decision.
